title: Publication-grade benchmark artefact with hardware and seed pinned
description:
Assemble the publication-grade benchmark artefact under `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/` consolidating all simulation outputs with hardware fingerprint, seed pins, and the figures from T27.

## Background

Epic success criterion 9: a reproducible benchmark artefact lives at `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/`, with hardware fingerprint, seed pins, and `scripts/permanent-repro.sh` runs end-to-end. This issue is the artefact assembly step — it consumes the epic's committed simulation outputs (S1, S1g, S2, S3, S5 — see Amendments §1: no S4 simulation exists in the epic; the S-series the epic produced is S1/S1g/S2/S3/S5) and produces a top-level `README.md` that pins the dataset.

The artefact directory layout:
- `README.md` — overview, hardware fingerprint, seed pins, figure index.
- `figures/` — output of T27.
- `csvs/` — S1/S1g/S2/S3/S5 CSVs (conventional names; frozen publication snapshot of the dated working CSVs).
- `provenance.json` — `artefact_assembly_commit`, per-dataset `dataset_source_commits`, rustc version, OS, ROCm version, hardware identifiers, seed pins.

(Criterion run data for this epic is recorded **inline in the CSV `#` headers**; the epic produced no standalone Criterion JSON output files, so there is no `criterion/` subdirectory — see Amendments §1.)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/README.md` exists, listing every CSV and figure included, and noting that Criterion run data is inline in the CSV headers (no standalone criterion JSONs / `criterion/` subdir — see Amendments §1).
- [ ] [hard] `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/provenance.json` records the artefact-assembly commit SHA, per-dataset source commits, `rustc --version`, `lscpu`, `rocminfo` (when available), and the seeds used.
- [ ] [hard] `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/figures/` is populated by T27's plot scripts.
- [ ] [hard] `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/csvs/` contains the S1/S1g/S2/S3/S5 CSVs with conventional names (amended 2026-05-17 from "S1-S5 CSVs"; see Amendments §1).
- [ ] [hard] User has signed off on the artefact (recorded as an `## Approval` section in the artefact README).

## Amendments (2026-05-17, user-approved via project-lead escalation)

1. **Scope corrected from "S1-S5" + `criterion/` to the epic's actual deliverables.** Reason: the issue was written at epic-breakdown time with speculative boilerplate ("consumes S1, S2, S3, S4, S5"; "`criterion/` copies of relevant Criterion JSON outputs"; "csvs/ — S1/S2/S3/S4/S5 CSVs"). The epic in fact produced the simulation series **S1, S1g, S2, S3, S5** — there is **no S4 simulation** anywhere in the epic (the dependency set 333028c1/424aa94f/4513209c/a9e461de/363556e6 contains no S4; verified). Criterion run data is recorded **inline in the CSV `#` headers**; the epic produced **no standalone Criterion JSON files**, so no `criterion/` subdirectory exists. Criterion 4 and the Background were amended accordingly (S1-S5 → S1/S1g/S2/S3/S5; criterion/ → inline-in-headers). No measurement is missing — the artefact bundles every simulation the epic actually produced. Approved by the user over the alternative ("investigate whether an S4 was intended" — confirmed none was).
